epics.title: Uploaded Document Hash Deduplication & Duplicate Registry Merge
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads enrollment, faculty, or curriculum files to the CRIE portal, I want SHA-256 content deduplication, duplicate-upload protection returning already extracted records, and lossless merging of legacy duplicate documents, so that the SQLite registry never accumulates duplicate document rows or breaks downstream links.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0 duplicate document rows inserted on repeat PDF uploads; 100% foreign-key link preservation after merging legacy IDs 1, 10, and 11
epics.tocConstraintRef: Repeated PDF uploads creating redundant document IDs and fragmenting linked contingent, faculty, and curriculum rows
requirements: R1: Compute deterministic content_sha256 digests (with normalized filename plus extracted text byte-size fallback check) in crie_document_engine.py and persist content_sha256 in an indexed/unique SQLite column on the documents table.

R2: Provide a database migration and cleanup script that takes a verified pre-migration SQLite backup, merges existing duplicate documents ID 1, 10, and 11 into a single canonical document ID without losing any foreign-key references across structured tables, and validates post-merge row integrity and rollback capability.

R3: Enforce duplicate-upload protection in crie_assistant_api.py so re-uploading a file with a matching hash creates no new document row and instead returns HTTP 200 with deduplicated=true, the existing document ID, the list of already-extracted structured DB records linked to it, and an explicit prompt/action to update or correct those records.
R4: Handle failed uploads and corrupt or empty files safely by returning clear 4xx/5xx feedback without inserting partial or orphaned document rows, leaving the registry clean for retry.
R5: Hand over cleanly from duplicate detection to the structured record editing workflow by exposing document-linked record summaries and edit targets in the upload response contract.

R6: Verify content hashing, legacy duplicate merge of IDs 1, 10, and 11, re-upload API deduplication (deduplicated=true), and error recovery across unit, integration, and API end-to-end tests using realistic CRIE PDF fixtures.

slices.title: Add content_sha256 Schema & Hashing in Document Engine
slices.jtbd: When implementing content hashing and SQLite schema updates for this epic, I want deterministic SHA-256 calculation and normalized fallback matching in crie_document_engine.py, so that duplicate uploads are reliably identified before insertion.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid PDF or DOCX upload stream in crie_document_engine.py, When the document registration helper processes the file, Then it computes content_sha256 plus normalized filename and extracted text size and persists them in the SQLite documents table.
Given an empty, unreadable, or corrupt file, When hashing or text extraction runs, Then the engine raises a typed validation error and commits zero partial rows to SQLite.
Given two uploads with identical bytes or matching normalized filename and text size, When lookup_existing_document is called, Then it deterministically resolves the canonical existing document record in under 10 ms.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Missing content_sha256 digest column and index on SQLite documents table
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% deterministic SHA-256 match accuracy across identical binary uploads and 0 partial DB inserts on malformed files

slices.title: Migrate & Merge Legacy Duplicate Document IDs 1, 10, and 11
slices.jtbd: When implementing legacy duplicate cleanup for this epic, I want an idempotent SQLite migration script under scripts/ that merges document IDs 1, 10, and 11 after backing up the database, so that all existing foreign-key relations stay intact without data loss.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a SQLite database containing duplicate document rows ID 1, 10, and 11 linked to structured records, When the migration script runs, Then it first writes a timestamped backup snapshot, backfills content_sha256 on all rows, and reassigns every dependent row from IDs 10 and 11 to canonical ID 1 within a single transaction.
Given a simulated foreign-key or SQLite constraint failure mid-merge, When the transaction aborts, Then the database rolls back cleanly to the pre-migration snapshot with zero lost links.
Given the script is executed a second time on an already migrated database, When it checks canonical state, Then it exits cleanly as a no-op with matching post-merge verification counts.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Split foreign-key references across existing duplicate document IDs 1, 10, and 11
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 orphaned child rows and 100% link preservation verified across pre/post migration counts

slices.title: Enforce Upload Deduplication & Record Summary in Assistant API
slices.jtbd: When implementing the upload endpoint guard for this epic, I want crie_assistant_api.py to intercept matching file hashes and return deduplicated=true with the original document ID and extracted DB records, so that callers never create duplicate documents and can immediately jump to correcting existing data.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an already-registered PDF uploaded again to the document upload endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py, When the backend detects a matching content_sha256 or normalized fallback key, Then it skips creating a new document row and returns HTTP 200 with deduplicated=true, existing document_id, extracted_records from SQLite, and an actionable prompt to update or correct those records.
Given a brand-new unique PDF upload, When the endpoint stores and parses the file, Then it returns deduplicated=false with the newly created document_id and extracted record summary.
Given a failed upload payload or unsupported/empty file, When the endpoint validates the request, Then it returns a structured 4xx JSON error with clear corrective guidance and leaves the documents table unchanged.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Upload endpoint unconditionally inserting new document records without hash lookup
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of repeat uploads returning deduplicated=true with original document_id and valid extracted_records payload

epics.title: Interactive Structured DB Record Viewing & Revision-Logged Correction
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads a file or selects an existing registry document (IDs 1-11), I want to inspect a card of extracted structured SQLite records (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula) and apply targeted corrections via API, UI, or chat commands with revision logging, so that institutional data is accurately maintained and immediately reflected in subsequent assistant responses.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of field corrections atomically persisted to SQLite with immutable revision logs and reflected on the very next agent turn
epics.tocConstraintRef: Static one-way PDF extraction with no API, UI, or chat mechanism to inspect and correct misparsed DB rows
requirements: R1: Implement structured SQLite CRUD operations and an immutable record_revisions audit table in crie_persistent_memory.py for enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula linked by document_id.

R2: Define a shared API contract and DTO schema (docs/contracts/ and Pydantic models) for fetching document-linked structured records, patching specific fields, viewing revision history, and confirming destructive changes ahead of parallel backend, agent, and UI work.

R3: Implement REST CRUD and revision-history endpoints in crie_assistant_api.py with strict field validation, clear error responses that never discard unsaved client input, and confirmation tokens/flags for destructive actions.

R4: Implement agent tools and response cards in crie_autonomous_agent.py (backed by crie_persistent_memory.py) that display extracted DB records on file upload or document selection (IDs 1-11) and execute chat correction commands (trainee full name, specialty, study/funding basis, PPS instructor link, RUP hours) directly in SQLite with revision logging.
R5: Ensure every assistant query reads live SQLite tables from crie_persistent_memory.py without stale caching so any corrected field immediately appears in the next assistant answer.

R6: Build a responsive browser card and inline table editor in src/main/resources/static/index.html and frontend/src/ usable on mobile and desktop, displaying clear success/failure feedback, preserving typed input on validation or network errors, confirming destructive actions, and meeting WCAG 2.1 Level AA (keyboard operability, visible focus, labelled controls, 4.5:1 text contrast).

R7: Seed and exercise realistic CRIE domain data (authentic Russian residency/postgraduate orders, specialties 31.08.35, 32.08.12, 31.08.19, federal-budget vs. paid-contract funding, real PPS and RUP entries) rather than placeholder test items.
R8: Verify SQLite persistence, revision audit trail, REST CRUD, chat-driven agent corrections, next-turn answer alignment, and mobile/desktop UI editing across unit, integration, and E2E tests.

epics.title: Structured Registry Correction & Grounded Answer Telemetry (GQM)
epics.jtbd: When operating the CRIE structured database correction workflow, I want Goal-Question-Metric telemetry tracking Goal: enabling operators to inspect and fix parsed contingent, faculty, and curriculum records directly in SQLite so assistant answers stay 100% accurate without manual DB edits, by answering Q1 (are extracted record cards surfaced completely for uploaded and registered documents?), Q2 (do chat and API corrections persist with revision logs and reflect in the immediate next assistant reply?), and Q3 (how often do correction commands fail validation or diverge from SQLite state?), so that correction effectiveness is objectively measured.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% GQM event capture on record card views, correction commits, and post-edit answer alignment checks
epics.tocConstraintRef: Blind spots in detecting failed chat corrections or stale post-edit assistant answers in production
requirements: R1: State and enforce the GQM measurement model strictly for the structured record correction outcome: Goal (zero manual SQL edits and 100% SQLite-aligned answers after correction), Q1 (card surfacing completeness), Q2 (correction commit and revision-log rate plus next-turn alignment), and Q3 (validation error and stale-answer mismatch rate), omitting any metrics not answering Q1-Q3.

R2: Emit GQM telemetry events from crie_persistent_memory.py, crie_assistant_api.py, and TelemetryMetricsService on record card display, correction commit/failure, and post-edit agent query verification.
R3: Expose aggregated Q1-Q3 metrics in the existing telemetry summary endpoint so operators can monitor correction workflow health.
R4: Verify GQM metric accuracy for successful edits, validation failures, and stale-read prevention via automated unit and integration tests in tests/test_telemetry_gqm.py.

epics.title: Jargon-Free Live Document Registry Help & Upload/Edit Guidance
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator or faculty user asks the CRIE assistant how to upload, edit, or use files, I want internal prompt-engineering jargon completely eliminated and replies dynamically grounded in live SQLite document lists and extracted table counts alongside clear step-by-step UI instructions, so that users see real system state and know exactly how to upload and correct records.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0 occurrences of banned prompt jargon ('slot to current replica' / 'system prompt') in user-facing replies; 100% match between cited document/table counts and live SQLite state
epics.tocConstraintRef: System prompts leaking internal LLM prompt-slot terminology instead of live DB statistics and actionable UI upload/edit steps
requirements: R1: Remove all internal prompt-engineering terminology (including Russian equivalents of 'slot to current replica' and 'system prompt') from system prompts and response templates across crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_autonomous_agent.py, and crie_thought_agent.py (creating or wiring crie_thought_agent.py cleanly into the pipeline), and enforce a runtime output guard rejecting banned jargon before returning responses.

R2: Build a live backend registry statistics provider querying SQLite for concrete uploaded documents (such as active residency and postgraduate enrollment orders) and exact extracted record counts across contingent (enrolled_trainees), PPS (pps_staff), and RUP (rup_curricula) tables.

R3: Route user questions about uploading, editing, and using files to a structured guidance formatter that outputs: (1) concrete uploaded documents and extracted record counts from SQLite, and (2) clear step-by-step UI instructions (attach-file button -> automatic parsing into DB tables -> review and edit fields in chat or table).

R4: Handle empty-registry or transient SQLite read failures cleanly without falling back to prompt jargon or fabricated numbers, reporting 0 documents (or temporary unavailability) alongside the step-by-step upload UI instructions and retry guidance.

R5: Verify across unit, integration, and end-to-end chat API tests (including the Russian query asking how to send files to correct data) that the reply contains zero banned jargon, cites live SQLite document and table statistics, and presents the upload/edit workflow steps.
